execution_context.trigger: runtime (client-side, during user checkout or form submission)
execution_context.file_location: injected third-party JavaScript on eCommerce checkout page

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads credit card input fields from the checkout page, then sends the values to a hardcoded external domain via HTTP POST, enabling credit card data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive payment information from user input fields and transmits it to an external server, which is a classic sign of a skimming attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal third-party scripts should not access or exfiltrate payment data; legitimate analytics or UI scripts do not transmit raw credit card numbers to unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may collect and transmit card data, but only to trusted, PCI-compliant endpoints and with user consent.
key_indicators: Outbound network requests to untrusted domains
Execution in the context of sensitive checkout pages

attack_chain.action: Malicious third-party JavaScript is injected into the eCommerce site, often via a supply chain compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimming code in the user's browser during checkout.

attack_chain.action: The injected code executes in the browser, harvesting credit card and PII from form fields.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Stolen data is sent to an external server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives and monetizes stolen payment information.

behavioral_signatures: Client-side JavaScript accessing payment or PII input fields
Outbound HTTP requests from checkout pages to untrusted or unknown domains
Dynamic injection of scripts from third-party or Nth-party sources
file_indicators: Unexpected or recently changed third-party JavaScript files
References to external scripts not present in the original codebase
network_indicators: POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the merchant or payment processor
Unusual traffic patterns from checkout pages to new or suspicious endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript on sensitive pages that accesses payment or PII fields and initiates outbound network requests to untrusted domains. Use content security policies (CSP) to restrict script sources, and employ runtime monitoring to detect unauthorized data exfiltration. Regularly audit third-party and Nth-party scripts for unexpected changes or new behaviors.
